en: The Apadāna of the Elder Opavuyha The Bījanī Chapter, Number Five I was once a merchant in the city of Benares, Possessing great wealth and abundant grain. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Teacher, The All-Knowing One, appeared in the world. Having set out from Benares, he went to Sāvatthī, And there he dwelt at Jetavana, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Hearing of the arrival of the Teacher, the Buddha, the Blessed One, I took my caravan and set out for Sāvatthī. On the way, I saw the Teacher, the Buddha, the Blessed One, Walking along the road with a retinue of monks. Seeing him, my heart was filled with joy; I approached the Teacher and paid him homage. Then I invited the Teacher, the Blessed One, To accept a meal on the morrow together with his monks. He accepted my invitation by remaining silent; Then, having honored him, I returned to my own home. When the night had passed, I prepared a fine meal, Both hard and soft, and set out a seat. I informed the Teacher, the Blessed One, of the time: "It is time, O Blessed One; the meal is ready. Accompanied by the monks, the Teacher, the Blessed One, Came to my house and sat upon the prepared seat. Having served the Teacher, the Blessed One, and the monks, I took a low stool and sat down before them. Seated there, I spoke these words to the Teacher: "O Blessed One, please accept this small measure of seed-grain. The Teacher, the Blessed One, the All-Knowing One, Out of compassion for me, accepted it. Having accepted it, he gave it to the monks; The monks, in turn, distributed it among themselves. As they ate, the seeds were scattered about; They fell upon the ground and grew into sprouts. Seeing those sprouts, I was filled with wonder; I thought: "How marvelous is the power of the Buddha! I took those seeds and planted them in my field; In due course, they grew into a great harvest. Because of that gift of seed-grain, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-Three. There I enjoyed divine pleasures for a long time, Until I passed away from that celestial existence. Through the ripening of that same deed, I was reborn in a wealthy family in Benares. Endowed with great wealth and abundant grain, I lived there in prosperity for many years. When I passed away from that human life, I was reborn in the world of men once more. In every birth, I possessed great wealth and grain; My storehouses were always full to overflowing. Having performed many deeds of merit, I eventually passed away from this life. By the power of that same wholesome karma, I have now attained the state of an Arhat. With a mind free from all defilements, I dwell in peace, having reached the goal. This is the fruit of that seed-grain offering; Thus did I attain the state of a Worthy One. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Opavuyha, The fifth in the Bījanī Chapter.
“To the Buddha Padumuttara,
I gave a noble steed;
having presented it to the Fully Enlightened One, I offered it.”
I returned to my own home.
There was one named Devala by name,
the foremost disciple of the Teacher.
The heir of the True Dhamma,
the Blessed One, burdened with his final existence, came into my presence.
"A well-bred horse is not permitted [to refuse];
having understood your intention,
the Visionary One consented."
Having caused a Sindhu horse, swift as the wind and fleet of foot,
to be presented to Buddha Padumuttara;
I endured what was difficult to endure.
Whichever womb I was reborn into—
whether among the gods or among humans—
My mind, swift as the wind, becomes patient;
it is a great gain for them, truly well-acquired.
Those who have received full ordination—
should the Buddha exist in the world, I would again wait upon him.
Twenty-eight times I was a king of great power,
a conqueror of the four quarters.
The lord of Jambusaṇḍa,
this is my final birth; my last existence is now unfolding.
I have attained the immovable state,
having abandoned victory and defeat.
Among the thirty-four thousand [beings],...
You are a Kṣatriya of great majesty,
a wheel-turning monarch of mighty power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Opavayha spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Opavayha.
